document_summary: City of Boston FAQ for tenants on the Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA), an ordinance requiring landlords to give tenants a rights notice and to copy the city on eviction and non-renewal notices (Boston, MA).

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources)
rules.requirement: A landlord ending a tenancy or declining to renew a lease must deliver a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the Notice to Quit. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or non-renewal notice, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the Office of Housing Stability.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with the Notice to Quit; copy to the Office of Housing Stability
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.interaction: Procedural notice requirement only; it does not restrict the grounds for eviction and is separate from state eviction law. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.citation: City of Boston Ordinances § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date taken from the FAQ statement 'The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.' The ordinance was passed in October 2020 (exact day not stated, so adoption_date is null). The ordinance is a notice-and-reporting requirement, not a just-cause limit; it is categorized under just_cause_eviction as the closest available category. Enforcement: warning for the first offense, then $300 per day. The source is an official FAQ summary of the ordinance.
